newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STUNNED BY ULIHRACH AT INDIAN WELLS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STUNNED BY ULIHRACH AT INDIAN WELLS.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras suffered his first defeat of 1997 when he was stunned by Bohdan Ulihrach of the Czech Republic at the Champions Cup on Wednesday.
Sampras, who took a 17-0 1997 match record into the second-round encounter, was ousted 7-6 (7-5) 7-5 by the 43rd-ranked Ulihrach.
The top seed had won his last four tournaments, including the Australian Open in January, and was victorious in his previous 34 hardcourt matches, dating back to last August in Cincinnati.
"You know it's not going to last forever," Sampras said of his hot streaks, "but you hope when you do lose, you lose to someone that outplays you.
"He played okay, but I didn't play well. That adds a little bit of salt to the wound when you don't play the way you should play," Sampras lamented.
Shortly after Sampras's shocking defeat, fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic followed the top seed out the door.
The big-serving Croatian was bounced 7-5 6-3 by American doubles specialist Jonathan Stark, who was named to the U.S. Davis Cup team earlier in the day.

Sixth seed Thomas Enqvist of Sweden, the last player to beat Sampras on a hard court before Wednesday, also joined the casualty list, falling 6-4 6-4 to American Chris Woodruff, a semifinalist last week at Scottsdale.

"Today I just don't feel I played the way I should," said Sampras, twice a champion here who had not lost to a player ranked below 30th in the world since last year's ATP Tour World Team Championships in Dusseldorf, when he was also beaten by Ulihrach.
The Czech was naturally delighted with his good fortune.
"You can imagine how nice it is to beat him because he won 20 matches in a row," Ulihrach said. "It's an unbelievable feeling."
Ulihrach had particular success playing to Sampras's weaker backhand side in the one hour and 28 minute match played in 102-degree (39 C) desert heat.
"I've always had a problem, even though I've won here a couple of times. I never thought I played all that great here because of the dry weather. I just played very tentative tennis," Sampras said.
Sampras squandered three set points in the 12th game as the first-set went to a tie-break after neither player was able to break the other's serve.

Ulihrach failed on his first set point in the tiebreaker at 6-4 by double faulting. But he got lucky on the next point when his forehand from the baseline nicked the net and tumbled over onto Sampras's side.
They traded service breaks in the opening two games of the second set and stayed on serve until the last game.
Then, serving at 30-30, Sampras netted a forehand half volley, before falling victim to a screeching forehand crosscourt passing shot on the final point.
"Well, it was pretty ugly today," Sampras said of his play.
